newsitem.title: USA: Converse Inc pessimistic about rest of '97.
newsitem.headline: Converse Inc pessimistic about rest of '97.

text.p: Converse Inc said Wednesday that it expects earnings for the second half of 1997 to be lower than it had previously expected, though it does see them higher than in 1996.

In a statement accompanying the release of second quarter earnings, Glenn Rupp, chief executive, said "We expect that our results in the second half of 1997 will continue to be impacted by reduced royalty income from the Pacific region, as well as the effects of a strong U.S. currency."

"Due to increased competition, coupled with the strategic decision to eliminate certain lower quality distribution channels in the Pacific region, we expect royalty income in the second half to be approximately $6 million below the $16.4 million in the second half of 1996. Additionally, we anticipate that the strength of the U.S. dollar will have a potential further negative impact of approximately $2 million To $4 million in the second half of 1997."

The company reported a pretax loss from continuing operations of $3.1 million in the second quarter, ended June 30, and a pretax loss from continuing operations of $7.6 million in the first half of 1997.
Rupp, however, added that he remains confident about 1998 and Converse's long-term prospects because of an overall increase in global demand.
